## PyFFmpegCore {{ tag }}: bounded batch execution

PyFFmpegCore remains a local-first beta. FFmpeg and FFprobe stay explicit
system dependencies. This patch fixes per-job timeout behavior for the Python
batch API and rejects non-finite timeout values.

### What changed

- `BatchRunner.run(..., policy=BatchPolicy(per_job_timeout_seconds=...))` now
  passes the configured deadline into every job's execution plan.
- Direct execution and batch policies reject NaN and infinite timeouts instead
  of silently running without an effective deadline.

### Verification

- Exact release artifact checks on Linux, macOS, and Windows with Python 3.10
  and 3.14: [release workflow]({{ release_run_url }})
- [Batch timeout behavior](https://othmaneblial.github.io/pyffmpegcore/batches/)
- [Compatibility policy](https://othmaneblial.github.io/pyffmpegcore/COMPATIBILITY/)
- [Full changelog](https://github.com/OthmaneBlial/pyffmpegcore/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1)

Timeouts bound how long the managed process runner waits. They do not sandbox
untrusted media or guarantee that external child processes have no side effects.
